checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the legs and feet are obscured by the perch, marking them as untestable. This is accurate; forcing a verdict on hidden anatomy would be hallucination. All visible checkpoints (Head, Body, Plumage) were correctly marked as present. The Router was not too lenient; the visible features strongly match the 'cock' taxonomy.
artifact_review: The Router identified background smearing (severity 1.5) and tail-pole fusion (severity 2.0). I agree with these findings but assess the tail-pole fusion as more significant than the Router did. The black tail feathers do not just 'blend slightly'; they exhibit a distinct lack of occlusion boundary where they overlap the vertical pole, appearing to merge into it rather than sit in front of it. This is a classic generative artifact of depth sorting failure. Additionally, the animal_pose_auditor reported an 88% low-confidence ratio. While this is largely due to domain shift (bird vs. mammal model), the specific confusion around the shoulder/wing junction (keypoints 5-10) correlates visually with the somewhat amorphous transition between the red hackles and the black body/wing area. The texture of the lower body plumage also lacks the distinct feather definition seen in the neck, appearing slightly 'painted' or melted. Therefore, I am increasing the artifact severity to reflect these structural/textural issues beyond simple background blur.
alignment_reasoning: Expert classifiers confirm 'cock' with high confidence (0.78 detection, top logit 7.27). All visible diagnostic checkpoints are met with high fidelity. Two checkpoints (legs/feet) are legitimately untestable due to occlusion, not generation failure. The image is a near-perfect semantic match.
artifact_reasoning: Router correctly flagged background noise and edge fusion. I upgraded the severity of the tail-pole fusion (occlusion failure) and noted additional textural softness/melting in the lower body plumage which correlates with the pose auditor's uncertainty in the wing region. These are moderate structural artifacts that prevent a perfect score but do not ruin the image.
key_defects: Tail feathers merge into background pole without clear occlusion boundary
Lower body plumage lacks distinct feather texture, appearing smeared/painted
Background foliage exhibits AI-style smearing and lack of vein structure
